findings.description: Checked all 10 questions field-by-field between baseline_bundle and runtime_bundle: stem, options (id+text+order), answer_kind, difficulty, difficulty_level, and private_grading.correct_option_id are identical in every case. The only differing fields are per-question source.uri (study/drafts/planet-paradoxes-20261010.legacy.json -> /app/quizzes/Science/planet_paradoxes_20261010.json), per-question revision.sha256, the quiz-level revision.sha256, bundle_sha256, bundle_version (2026.10.10.planets-r1 -> 2026.10.11.planets), and published_at. This matches the declared migration scope.

revision.number stays 1 (both quiz-level and all 10 question-level) even though revision.sha256 changes between baseline and runtime. Not a content defect, but if downstream tooling treats revision.number as the change signal rather than the hash, the migration could be invisible to it.

For all 10 articles, binding_map.old_sha256 exactly matches the article_sha256 recorded for the same article_id in prior_primary_source_reviews, and each article's question_refs.revision_sha256 exactly matches the corresponding runtime_bundle (not baseline) question revision.sha256 -> articles are correctly re-bound to the new runtime revisions. binding_map.new_sha256 values were not independently recomputed (no hashing tool available in this review context); they are taken as supplied, consistent with the packet_sha256 handling instruction.

No ambiguity, multiple-correct-option, or giveaway-distractor issues found in the 10 Q/A sets. Spot-checked the flagged risk areas: Q9 correctly isolates Venus sidereal rotation (~243d) > orbital period (~225d, 'год'), with solar day (~116.75d) distractors made false by the arithmetic, so the Venus solar-vs-sidereal distinction is unambiguous. Q7 correctly separates Triton's retrograde orbital direction from Neptune's axial rotation (orbital vs axial motion). Q8 names the Great Red Spot an atmospheric anticyclone/storm, not a surface feature. Q10 separates 'no solid surface for landing' from the existence of a dense core (gas-giant core distinction), consistent with Q5's density discussion for Saturn. No independent fetch of NASA sources was performed in this pass; this relies on the cited prior reviewers' recorded evidence plus manual arithmetic/domain-knowledge sanity checks, not a fresh source open.

limitations: No tool, file, or network access in this review: packet_sha256 and all binding_map.new_sha256 values are taken as supplied, not independently recomputed.
Primary NASA sources were not fetched in this pass; factual checks rely on domain knowledge plus the evidence already recorded by prior reviewers who stated they opened those sources.
Field comparisons between baseline_bundle and runtime_bundle were done by manual text comparison of the provided JSON, not an automated diff tool.
This is a content/migration review only; no release approval is given or implied.
